text:
Aisha Gomez: Hi team, placement date for our foster-to-adopt just came through (probable in ~6 weeks). I'm trying to get the timeline right for paperwork, retroactive benefits for the child, and whether payroll/top-up can be prorated if I start leave mid-pay-cycle. Also need a 1-paragraph handoff my manager can post.

Sam (Manager): Congrats Aisha!! Quick pragmatic Qs: do you know whether placement is a "placement for adoption" qualifying event or finalization? Timing matters for when benefits become effective.

Aisha Gomez: It's placement for adoption — we expect a placement letter from the agency before placement and finalization may be months later.

Tanya (People Ops): Congrats Aisha :tada: Short answers: placement-for-adoption is a qualifying event that allows enrollment of the child in medical/dental within 30 days of placement. You can e-sign enrollment forms now and upload placement letter later.

Tanya (People Ops): Payroll/top-up: we can do a prorated top-up that starts the first payroll after your leave start. To hit that payroll cycle, submit the leave start date at least 21 business days before. If you're within that window we'll still do retro pay for the top-up once dates are confirmed.

Tanya (People Ops): Documentation we need: agency placement letter (upload when received), completed benefits enrollment form (DocuSign ok), and the leave request form for our system. If you anticipate FMLA leave, file the FMLA packet within 15 days of your leave start or the packet date we send.

benefits-bot: Benefits enrollment reminder sent. Form link: https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/benefits-enroll (DocuSign).

Aisha Gomez: Can you clarify "retro pay" — will it show up as a separate line-item? I need to reconcile with personal finances.

Tanya (People Ops): Yes, retro top-up will appear as a separate adjustment on the payroll following confirmation. We'll code it as "Parental Leave Top-up - Retro" and provide a breakdown. Finance will email you the calculation once HR confirms earnings dates.

Sam (Manager): For coverage, Aisha, would you like two-week overlap or a one-week overlap + doc walkthroughs? I can post the handoff message once you paste a short paragraph.

Aisha Gomez: Two-week overlap preferred. Please include that in the handoff. Here's a 1-paragraph handoff I drafted:

"Aisha will be on parental leave from START_DATE to END_DATE. For urgent infra or oncall issues, please contact Sam (sam@redwood.com). For ongoing projects: - Feature X: see PRs at <link>. - Quarterly roadmap items: OWNER_1 and OWNER_2. Aisha will do a 2-week overlap for knowledge transfer starting OVERLAP_START. For anything off-hours contact the on-call rotation listed in the runbook: <link>."

Sam (Manager): Perfect, I'll post that and add the on-call rotation.

Tanya (People Ops): A couple more operational things: we can reserve the lactation room and set up temporary parking for medical visits—reply here with preferred dates. Also note: your dependent's coverage is effective from placement date if you enroll within 30 days; if you miss that window coverage can be backdated in special circumstances but may require a benefits appeal.

Aisha Gomez: I'll upload the placement letter when it arrives. One last thing — equipment handoff: can people-ops trigger laptop checkout for a contractor covering 12 weeks?

Tanya (People Ops): Yes. Send contractor start/end dates and we will coordinate IT and asset checkout. We'll also flag the account access expiry so there are no lingering privileges.

benefits-bot: HR ticket opened: HR-PL-2026-332. People Ops will follow up with the enrollment packet in 1 business day.

Aisha Gomez: Thanks all 8536; appreciate the quick responses. I'll update here when I have the placement letter.
